question: The mode and median of a data set is 14.2 and 60, respectively. What is the mean of the data set? (Use empirical formula.)
solution: __Shortcut Trick__ Apply the **Empirical Formula**: **Mean = (3 × Median − Mode) ÷ 2**. Mean = (3 × 60 − 14.2) ÷ 2 Mean = (180 − 14.2) ÷ 2 Mean = 165.8 ÷ 2 = 82.9 **∴ The correct answer is 82.9.** **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** **Mode** of the data set = 14.2 **Median** of the data set = 60 **Formula Used:** The **Empirical Formula** for a moderately skewed distribution is: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/504fc5715517174c6adab68e6fe2b4aa8a3eb99aa62930e696eb7701f5e816c7.png] **Calculations:** ⇒ 14.2 = 3 × 60 − 2 × Mean ⇒ 14.2 = 180 − 2 × Mean ⇒ 2 × Mean = 180 − 14.2 ⇒ 2 × Mean = 165.8 ⇒ Mean = 165.8 ÷ 2 ⇒ Mean = 82.9 **∴ The correct answer is 82.9.** **__Additional Information__** Empirical Relationship The **empirical relationship** between Mean, Median, and Mode is used for **unimodal** and **moderately skewed** distributions.
